creditor

Source: CLAUDE.md

R package that wraps the loro Rust crate to expose Loro CRDT documents to R. Exploratory. The build and binding layout mirrors the sibling q2r package.

Architecture

Rust

  • src/rust/src/lib.rs exposes thin #[extendr] functions named loro_*_impl, tagged /// @noRd so they are not R-exported. Fallible calls return extendr_api::Result, which surfaces as an R error.
  • Two pointer types cross the boundary: ExternalPtr<LoroDoc> for documents and ExternalPtr<loro::Container> for every container handle. Using the Container enum (rather than one pointer type per container) keeps a single handle type; each function unwraps the variant it needs via as_text / as_map / as_movable_list / as_counter / as_tree and errors on a mismatch. LoroList and LoroMovableList share method names but no trait, so the shared loro_list_* functions dispatch over both with the with_list! macro. New containers are created detached (detached_container, the one place that lists the creatable kinds) and attached with insert_container / set_container (loro_*_attach_impl), which copies the detached contents, nested detached children included, into the document. Loro records the attached copy on the detached object; loro_container_resolve_impl swaps a handle’s Container for it in place, so every R reference to the external pointer follows the container into the document.
  • A handle is returned to R by container_ref as list(kind, ptr) with class creditor_container_ref. Functions that can return either a plain value or a child container (loro_map_get_impl, loro_list_get_impl) go through value_or_container_to_r; the class is what lets R tell the two apart, since plain values never carry one. Text, map, list, movable list, counter, and tree are supported; an unknown container type falls back to its deep value on read.
  • src/rust/src/container_value.rs produces container and document values (container_to_r, doc_to_r) by walking the handles, not by converting get_deep_value(). A LoroValue no longer records which container each part came from, so a tree node’s 0-based index could not be told apart from a map entry named index; the walker knows the type and emits tree nodes with 1-based index and NA root parents. Items are collected from for_each before any child is read, so no Loro iteration is open while another container is accessed. The deep flag switches child containers between expanded contents and id strings. Diffs and subscription events still use get_deep_value() for inserted child containers (they are built while Loro is emitting an event, where reading other containers is not safe), so a tree nested inside a diff insert keeps Loro’s raw form.
  • src/rust/src/value_to_r.rs converts a LoroValue into nested R lists (map keys sorted for stable output; I64 becomes an integer when it fits and is not NA_integer_, else a double).
  • src/rust/src/r_to_value.rs is the inverse, for values stored with map_set / list_insert: NULL and NA become null, length-one atomic vectors become scalars, other unnamed vectors and lists become lists, named ones become maps, raw becomes binary, and anything with a class attribute is rejected. Zero-length vectors are handled before any slice is taken, because building a slice from an empty R vector’s data pointer panics (and aborts R) in debug builds.
  • src/rust/src/delta.rs converts between Vec<TextDelta> and the R delta shape (a list of ops, each a named list with one of retain / insert / delete plus optional attributes). Delta counts are Unicode code points, like every other text index.
  • Rich text: mark keys must be present in the document’s StyleConfigMap or mark fails with “Style configuration missing”. loro_doc_config_text_style_impl always starts from StyleConfigMap::default_rich_text_config() (bold, italic, underline, link, highlight, comment, code) and overlays the caller’s keys, because config_text_style replaces the whole map and there is no getter to merge with. Keys containing : are rejected up front since StyleConfigMap::insert panics on them.
  • Cursors cross as Cursor::encode() bytes and are resolved with LoroDoc::get_cursor_pos. LoroText::get_cursor does not reject an out-of-range position (it silently returns an end cursor), so the range check lives in R. List cursors (loro_list_cursor_impl) work on both list types, but Loro cannot resolve a cursor on a movable-list element once that element has been moved (get_cursor_pos fails with “Cannot find relative position”); this is documented and pinned by a test.
  • src/rust/src/history.rs converts a DiffBatch (text, list, and map diffs; child containers by deep value; other types as unsupported) and the change log (travel_change_ancestors from the oplog frontiers, sorted by lamport then peer) to R. The diff’s type field is emitted as type_ because type is a Rust keyword inside list!; R renames it. Versions for history cross as Frontiers::encode() bytes; a change’s frontiers is the id of its last op.
  • doc_frontiers() reports state_frontiers() (what the document is showing), which differs from the oplog frontiers while detached. A detached document is read-only (detached editing is not enabled).
  • src/rust/src/events.rs implements subscriptions as queues, not direct callbacks. Loro’s subscriber closure converts each event to an R object and pushes it onto an EventQueue; R later drains the queue with loro_subscription_take_impl and calls the user’s function. This keeps R code (which can error, or re-enter Loro) from ever running inside a Loro commit or import. EventQueue has unsafe impl Send + Sync because Loro requires it of subscribers while Robj is neither; this is sound only because every Loro call happens on R’s main thread. Do not introduce threads without revisiting it.
  • The ephemeral store is an ExternalPtr<loro::awareness::EphemeralStore>, independent of any document. Its two subscription kinds reuse QueuedSubscription. Inside loro_ephemeral_get_impl the pointer is first re-borrowed as &EphemeralStore, because calling .get() on the ExternalPtr resolves to extendr’s GetSexp::get instead of Loro’s method; watch for this with any Loro method named get.
  • Detached editing (set_detached_editing) is a per-object runtime switch. While it is on, Loro assigns a fresh random peer id at every checkout and keeps it after re-attaching; edits made at an old version become a concurrent branch that merges on doc_checkout(doc).
  • Text positions can be converted between units with LoroText::convert_pos (unicode, utf16, and utf8 map to PosType::Unicode / Utf16 / Bytes). The R side keeps positions 1-based in every unit. A mid-character offset converts to the start of that character; only out-of-range offsets give NA.
  • An explicit commit timestamp is stored even when timestamp recording is off, and Loro forces timestamps to be non-decreasing, so later commits without one inherit the latest stored value.
  • subscribe_first_commit_from_peer fires only for local commits (once per peer id this document commits under), not for imported peers.
  • Commit origins (set_next_commit_origin) are local labels: they reach subscribers as event$origin and are matched by prefix against an undo manager’s excluded origins, but are not stored in history. Loro labels the commits made by undo and redo with origin "undo".
  • Undo is a plain ExternalPtr<UndoManager>; undo / redo return whether anything changed. Loro clears the undo and redo stacks on checkout.
  • Sync extras in lib.rs: loro_doc_export_impl also handles shallow_snapshot (encoded frontiers in since); imports return an ImportStatus converted by status_to_r to column-wise success / pending ranges; JSON updates are serialized with serde_json (a direct dependency for that reason); JSONPath needs the jsonpath feature of the loro crate. loro_doc_apply_diff_impl computes the DiffBatch in a source document and applies it in the same call, so no diff object has to cross into R (the R list from doc_diff() is lossy: child containers appear by value).
  • More Loro behaviors worked around: unparseable JSON passed to import_json_updates surfaces an unrelated “no active undo group” error, so the JSON is converted to a JsonSchema first and a clear error raised; LoroList::pop returns a child container as a bare id, so loro_list_pop_impl reads the deep value before deleting; ensure_mergeable_* on a key that already holds a mergeable container of another type silently creates a second container under the same key, so loro_map_ensure_container_impl checks the existing type first.
  • to_r_error strips the Position: <source path> suffix and the at <path>.rs:LINE:COL suffix (Unix or Windows path) Loro appends to some error messages.
  • Robustness rules learned from reviewing against Loro’s own tests (each has a test):
    • Strings: extendr exposes an R string’s bytes as &str unchecked, and Loro panics on invalid UTF-8, poisoning the document’s mutex (later calls fail, and R can abort at exit). Every string therefore goes through as_utf8() in R (check_string) or utf8_strings() in Rust (r_to_value.rs, also used for names and delta inserts): translate with enc2utf8, then validate. Never read a user string with as_str() / as_ref() directly.
    • Recursion: r_to_value and the container walker cap nesting at 1000 levels and return an error. Unbounded recursion overflows the C stack, which R reports as an uncatchable segfault; if it happens inside Loro while a lock is held the process can also hang at exit.
    • Bounds: positions and ranges for text and lists are checked in R (check_insert_pos, check_element_pos, check_positions, check_range in R/utils.R), and tree indexes in Rust (check_tree_index), so errors name the 1-based value the caller passed. Loro’s own messages are 0-based and sometimes report the end of a range, and Loro skips the bounds check for zero-length ranges. Range arithmetic is done in doubles to avoid integer overflow.
    • Versions: doc_version() returns class loro_version and doc_frontiers() / doc_changes()$frontiers class loro_frontiers (raw vectors underneath). The encodings overlap, so Loro decodes one as the other without error and silently uses a different version; check_version / check_frontiers prevent that. Anywhere frontiers are expected, check_frontiers(x, arg, doc) also accepts a change number (in doc_changes() order) or a commit message, resolved against that document’s history (source’s for doc_apply_diff) and returned as frontiers; callers must use its return value. A message that matches no change or several is an error. Indexing doc_changes() (changes$frontiers[[1]], changes[1, ]) is deliberately not the documented way to name a version.
    • revert_to and apply_diff write into the open transaction without committing; the bindings commit afterwards so the change reaches subscribers, undo, and live sync.
    • Map diffs report updated (keys set, possibly to NULL) separately from deleted (keys removed).
    • Trees: a node inside a deleted subtree is not live. Loro would let it be moved (reviving the subtree) or deleted; to_live_node rejects both.
    • undo_group() commits pending edits before the group starts and before it ends (the manager object keeps the document pointer for this); otherwise edits inside the group merge into whatever is committed next.
    • JSON: doc_export_json() refuses a document whose JSON contains the marker Loro 1.18 writes for a map_ensure_container() child ("value":[0,76,77,1,...]), because importing it corrupts the receiving replica. This is an upstream bug; recheck it when bumping loro.
  • Trees: node ids cross as TreeID’s display form ("counter@peer"), parsed back with TreeID::try_from; a root-level parent is NULL going in and NA coming out. Three Loro behaviors are worked around or documented. LoroTree::children returns None for a leaf as well as for a missing node, so loro_tree_children_impl checks existence itself. Loro allows a deleted node as the parent of a create or move (the node lands in the deleted part of the tree), which to_live_parent rejects. Undoing or reverting a node deletion recreates the subtree under new node ids.
  • Positions in Rust are 0-based (text positions are Unicode code point indices via LoroText::insert / delete / len_unicode). Peer ids are u64 and cross as decimal strings. Versions cross as VersionVector::encode() bytes.
  • src/rust/document.rs is the document binary that regenerates R/extendr-wrappers.R on every build. New functions must be listed in the extendr_module! block.

R

  • R/doc.R defines the exported S7 class loro_doc (a @ptr slot holding the external pointer, so documents have reference semantics, and a @state environment for R-side state shared by every reference to the document) and the doc_* functions: identity, fork, commit, deep value, path queries (doc_get, which walks the handles in R one step per argument with 1-based list positions, and doc_jsonpath, whose expression keeps JSONPath’s 0-based positions), and sync (doc_export / doc_export_updates / doc_export_shallow, one function per export mode so no argument depends on another, plus doc_import / doc_version, doc_merge for two documents in one session (an R-level import of doc_export_updates(source, from = doc); from accepts a document as its version), JSON updates, blob_metadata). doc_import / doc_merge / doc_import_json return the document so they pipe; the status of the most recent import is stored in doc@state$import_status and read with doc_import_status(). A plain attribute on the returned object would not work, because callers who do not capture the result would never see it.
  • R/container.R defines the S7 handle classes: abstract loro_container (unexported) with children loro_text, loro_map, loro_list, loro_counter, and loro_tree, plus loro_movable_list as a child of loro_list (so every list_* function accepts it, while list_move / list_set require it). The child classes are exported because their constructors create new detached containers with initial contents (loro_list("a", "b"), loro_text("hi")); internally a handle is wrapped with the .ptr argument instead. A new container is stored wherever a value is (map_store / list_store / list_set, via attachable). container_ptr (and handle_ptr for functions that do not accept a document) resolves a detached handle that has since been attached, so every container function must get its pointer through one of them rather than reading @ptr directly. Users get handles from doc_text() / doc_map() / doc_list() / doc_movable_list() / doc_counter() / doc_tree() (root containers) or from a parent container; container_from_ref turns a Rust creditor_container_ref into the matching class and passes plain values through. Also holds container_value(), container_id(), and the shared print method.
  • R/text.R, R/map.R, R/list.R, R/counter.R, and R/tree.R define the text_*, map_*, list_*, counter_*, and tree_* functions, each taking a handle as its first argument. The R API is 1-based; the conversion to 0-based happens here. New child containers come from the loro_*() constructors and are stored like plain values; there are no type-name container creators.
  • R/richtext.R defines text_mark / text_unmark / text_delta / text_apply_delta and doc_config_text_style; with_style_hint rewrites Loro’s missing-style error (which names the JS API) to point at doc_config_text_style(). text_delta() returns class loro_delta (a plain list underneath; text_apply_delta() unclasses it). R/render.R renders deltas. text_ansi() styles each run with cli and returns a cli::ansi_string; text_markdown() / text_html() turn the runs into open/close tokens with a stack, opening the mark that lasts longest outermost so tags nest, and Markdown moves spaces outside ** / * / link delimiters, which would otherwise not parse. All three take marks, user renderers by key (two strings or a function of the value for Markdown and HTML, a styling function for ANSI) checked by check_renderers; a key with a renderer is never reported as dropped, and given Markdown delimiters get the same space shifting as the built-in ones. Marks a format cannot show make text_markdown() / text_ansi() warn once per call (class creditor_dropped_marks; strict = TRUE errors). A delta prints as its Markdown rendering, or another one chosen by print(x, format =) or the creditor.delta_format option; its format / print methods are registered through S7 like the package’s other print methods (see R/history.R), and str() is an S3 method that drops the class. R/cursor.R defines text_cursor, list_cursor, and cursor_pos; a cursor is a plain raw vector, like a version from doc_version().
  • R/history.R defines doc_frontiers, doc_changes (a tibble with a frontiers list column), doc_change, the counts, doc_changed_containers, the conversions between frontiers and version vectors, doc_compare_frontiers, doc_checkout, doc_is_detached, doc_revert_to, doc_diff, doc_apply_diff, and doc_record_timestamps.
  • R/events.R holds the subscription registry (the the environment: id to list(ptr, callback)) and deliver_events(). Delivery has three properties that tests pin and that must be kept. (1) Every exported function that takes a document or undo manager registers on.exit(deliver_events(), add = TRUE) right after checking its argument, so events are delivered whichever Loro call committed them (many read-only calls commit implicitly, e.g. doc_changes) and also when the call errors after committing. A new doc_* function must do the same; test-events.R loops over the committing functions. (2) Events are moved from the Rust queues onto one R-side FIFO (the$pending) and delivered from there; a nested deliver_events() (a callback that commits) only enqueues and returns, which keeps events in order. An event leaves the FIFO just before its callback runs, so an interrupted delivery loses nothing. (3) deliver_events() first asks Rust whether anything is queued at all (loro_events_pending_impl, a global atomic counter), so a call that produced no events costs the same however many subscriptions exist. Callback errors become warnings. The registry keeps a subscription alive until unsubscribe().
  • R/ephemeral.R defines the ephemeral_* functions. Loro’s Rust API does not expire entries on a timer (the JS wrapper does), so expiry is only applied when ephemeral_remove_outdated() is called. Entries are last-write-wins on a millisecond timestamp, and a receiving store drops a write that is not strictly newer, so two writes to one key in the same millisecond leave receivers stale; tests that sync successive writes to one key must sleep between them (tick() in test-ephemeral.R).
  • R/undo.R defines doc_undo_manager, undo, redo, can_undo, can_redo, the step counts, undo_group, pause and resume, and undo_clear.
  • Tabular results (doc_changes, doc_change, tree_nodes, the import status) are tibbles built with tibble::tibble(), never base data frames. A value that has to appear in them must print meaningfully: loro_frontiers formats as the counter@peer ids of its operations (loro_frontiers_ids_impl) and registers pillar::obj_sum so list-column cells show the same. If a column needs hiding to make output readable, fix its display or drop it instead.
  • R/utils.R holds the argument checks (cli::cli_abort(), with call = rlang::caller_env()), and named_values() / unnamed_values(), which collect dynamic dots (rlang::list2()). A function whose ... takes user-chosen keys as argument names (map_set, ephemeral_set, text_mark, doc_config_text_style) gives every other argument before ... a leading dot (.map, .store, .text / .start / .end, .doc), because R matches a named argument exactly and partially against those formals, so a key such as map, st, or e would otherwise be taken as the argument. The checks take an arg (or args) name so their errors name the dotted argument.
  • Interface conventions, which new functions should follow:
    • Keyed writes take key = value pairs in ... (map_set, ephemeral_set, text_mark, doc_config_text_style); sequence writes take unnamed values in ..., one element each (list_push, list_insert). Both loop over a single-value Rust call, so a rejected value leaves the earlier ones applied. An argument that sits beside named dots gets a dot prefix (.default).
    • map_delete and ephemeral_delete take keys in ... as any number of character vectors (key_dots); map_has and text_unmark take one character vector; list_delete takes a vector of positions and deletes contiguous runs from the end backward.
    • Text ranges are start / end, inclusive, as in substr(); an empty range is end = start - 1. check_range converts to the 0-based half-open range Rust expects.
    • Durations are in seconds (ephemeral_store(timeout), doc_undo_manager(merge_interval)) and converted to Loro’s milliseconds by check_seconds.
    • Every function that takes a container handle also accepts a loro_doc, which stands for its root container of that type under the default name (text_insert(doc, 1, "a") is text_insert(doc_text(doc), 1, "a")). container_ptr() does this: container functions start with ptr = container_ptr(x, class, "x") and pass ptr to Rust, and still return the argument they were given. A document stands for its plain list, so the movable-list functions reject one. The base generic methods are for handles only.
    • Handles have methods for base generics, registered with S7::method(): length (text, map, list), names / $ / [[ / $<- / [[<- (map), [[ / [[<- (list; assignment needs a movable list), as.character (text), as.list (map, list). The assignment methods return the handle, and assigning NULL deletes (map$key = NULL, list[[pos]] = NULL), as with an R list; map_set(map, key = NULL) is the way to store a null. map$child$key = value makes R assign the child handle back to child; is_same_child turns that step into a no-op; any other handle that is already in a document is rejected (abort_attached), while a new detached one is stored. The empty string is a valid map key that ... cannot express, so map[[""]] = value is the way to write it.
  • Pipeable editing functions are a primary goal of the API. Every exported function is one of three kinds: editors change something and return their first argument invisibly (all text_* / map_* / list_* / counter_* / tree_* edits, doc_import*, doc_merge, doc_commit, doc_checkout, the doc_set_* functions, undo / redo / undo_group, the ephemeral_* setters); constructors create something new and return it (loro_doc, the loro_* container constructors, doc_fork, doc_undo_manager, the doc_subscribe* functions, ephemeral_store, and tree_create, which returns the new node id); and accessors and predicates return a value without changing anything (*_get, *_length, doc_value, can_undo, doc_is_*, and so on; list_pop counts as an accessor that also removes). An editor never returns a status: an extra outcome is stored with the object and read through an accessor (doc_import_status()), and a no-op that callers may want to catch is reported by a strict argument that turns it into an error (undo, redo, undo_group).

Toolchain

  • Rust edition 2024, rustc >= 1.85 (declared in DESCRIPTION via SystemRequirements). Bridge: extendr-api 0.9.
  • Crates are fetched by cargo at build time (no vendoring; not CRAN-targeted). src/rust/Cargo.lock is committed.
  • README.md is generated: edit README.qmd and run quarto render README.qmd with the current package installed, so the example output is real. It renders to GitHub markdown with wrap: none and smart off: prose is never hard wrapped, and only code comments in the chunks may be wrapped (within 100 characters).
  • Rebuild after Rust edits with devtools::document(); set the DEBUG=1 environment variable for a fast unoptimized build (the release profile uses LTO and is slow).
  • tools/config.R and tools/msrv.R run at install time from configure to check the toolchain and template src/Makevars{,.win}.in. They are rextendr-generated; do not restyle or remove them.

Style

  • R: use = for assignment, pkg::fn over imports, minimize single-line comments. In examples, the README, and vignettes, chain edits with the native pipe (|>), one step per line, but only when there are at least two steps: a single call on a variable is a plain call (text_push(a, "x"), not a |> text_push("x")). Within a chunk, leave a blank line after any code that prints output before the next code, so each result sits visibly with the code that produced it.
  • Rust: standard rustfmt; no decorative comments.
  • Commit messages: one short imperative line, no attribution trailers.
